body:
Doctrine **8.a** (ratified) says the 100% sovereign path is always the number one
preferred way to run this code, and that paid platforms are never prioritized.

#277 took the first step: both sovereign lanes are now **on by default**, gated on a
readiness probe so they can never queue against an offline runner. But the sovereign
lane is still structurally a *fallback* — it runs only when the paid review returned
**no verdict at all**. Under 8.a, that ordering is backwards.

## Why it was not simply inverted in #277

The local verdict is narrower **by construction**, and this is a real capability floor
rather than a preference:

- constrained decoding guarantees the output *shape*, not the *judgment*;
- it reviews the **diff only** — the documentation-contract fields are not evaluated at
  all.

Doctrine 10's decomposition clarification is the right tool here: decompose the review
into the parts each lane can actually carry, rather than choosing one lane for the whole
job.

## Proposed shape

1. **Split the review contract** into what is diff-groundable (the sovereign lane can
   carry this in full) and what requires the wider context (documentation contract,
   cross-file reasoning).
2. **Sovereign goes first** on the diff-groundable half whenever the probe reports ready.
3. **Paid runs** for the remainder — and only for the remainder — so a healthy sovereign
   lane *reduces* paid spend rather than being bypassed by it.
4. **Gate composition**: the published verdict states which lane carried which half, so a
   human can always see what was actually evaluated and by what.
5. The paid lane remains the fallback for the sovereign half when the probe says not
   ready — the current relationship, inverted.

## Acceptance

- with a fresh heartbeat and credits available, the diff review is carried by the
  sovereign lane and the paid call is measurably smaller;
- with no heartbeat, behaviour is exactly today's;
- with no credits, behaviour is exactly #277's;
- the gate names the lane behind each half of the verdict;
- 100% coverage maintained.

Made with ❤️ by [Vibey](https://adammatthewsteinberger.github.io/vibey/), Developed by [Adam Matthew Steinberger](https://vibewithadam.matthewsteinberger.com/) ([@adammatthewsteinberger](https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/)).

The usual cause is a request too large to complete in one attempt — several distinct changes asked for together, or a wide audit before any of them. Splitting it into separate issues, each with its own acceptance criteria, makes each one solvable. Infrastructure failures such as an exhausted API credit balance produce the same symptom; the run log distinguishes them.

## Triage — 2026-09-17 (`develop` @ f2467910, v0.8.0)

**Status: NOT STARTED** · size **L** · confidence high

**The ask, as read:** Split the PR review contract into a diff-groundable half and a wider-context half, run the sovereign lane FIRST on the diff-groundable half, shrink the paid call to the remainder, and have the gate name which lane carried which half.

### What already ships
- Item 1: the review contract is split into diff-groundable and requires-wider-context halves, in one named, constructible, tested place (review_contract.py), with an interface declaration and a drift test that holds it against the shipped workflow schema
- The local reviewer now derives its schema, its unevaluated field set and its 'NOT evaluated' notice from that contract instead of restating them
- Half of item 4: the published gate already names the local model and says the documentation-contract fields were not evaluated — but only in the fallback-ran case, for the whole verdict
- The prerequisite from #277: the sovereign lane is enabled by default and gated on a fresh heartbeat so it can never queue against an offline runner

### Evidence in the tree
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/review_contract.py:1-160 — ReviewContract with DIFF_GROUNDABLE=('pass','summary','findings') (:43), the 16 documentation-contract fields as REQUIRES_WIDER_CONTEXT (:50-68), placeholders() (:147) and unevaluated_notice (:70-74); overlapping halves raise (:113)
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/local_review.py:30,55,64,202,204 — the local reviewer derives its schema's required list, UNEVALUATED_FIELDS, the notice and the placeholders from REVIEW_CONTRACT (live consumer, not a test-only import)
- src/vibey_tools/gh/test/test_review_contract.py:45 — asserts set(REVIEW_CONTRACT.fields) == set(schema['required']) of the PRIMARY schema in pr-automation.yml, i.e. the paid reviewer is still asked for all 19 fields
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/templates/workflows/pr-automation.yml:1176-1198 — job is still named `review-fallback`, `needs: [evaluate, review]`, and gated on `needs.review.result == 'failure' && needs.review.outputs.passed == ''`
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/templates/workflows/pr-automation.yml:238-242 — the paid `review` job has `needs: evaluate` only and runs on every ready/review PR; it never waits on, or is narrowed by, the sovereign lane
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/templates/workflows/pr-automation.yml:1352-1376 — the gate does name the reviewer when the fallback ran ('PR automation: gate (local fallback)', 'It reviewed the DIFF ONLY'), but for the whole verdict, not per-half
- …and 4 more

### What is actually left
- Add a `review-sovereign` job in templates/workflows/pr-automation.yml that runs when `needs.evaluate.outputs.sovereign_ready == 'true'` WITHOUT depending on the paid `review` result, carrying only REVIEW_CONTRACT.diff_groundable; keep the trusted_only fork exclusion and the no-secrets/no-checkout posture the current fallback has
- Generate the paid review job's `--json-schema` from review_contract instead of hardcoding the 19-field object, and narrow it to REQUIRES_WIDER_CONTEXT when the sovereign half returned a verdict (acceptance: 'the paid call is measurably smaller')
- Make the paid lane the fallback for the diff-groundable half only when the heartbeat is stale — invert the current `needs.review.outputs.passed == ''` relationship
- Compose the two verdicts in the `gate` job: one conclusion, plus a summary that names the lane behind each half (item 4 as written), with separate pass/findings inputs per half
- Carry a configured ReviewContract to both reviewers (read from .vibey-gh.toml) rather than importing the module-level REVIEW_CONTRACT singleton — review_contract.py:80-87 names this as the follow-up
- Add the three acceptance matrices as tests: fresh heartbeat + credits, no heartbeat, no credits; plus the rendered-template drift check tools-lint already runs
- Maintain vibey-gh's own 100% branch gate on the changed modules
- Lane ordering unchanged: the paid exact-head review still runs first and unconditionally (pr-automation.yml:238-241), and the sovereign lane still runs only when the paid lane returned no verdict at all (:1187-1195). Acceptance bullet 1 ("with a fresh heartbeat and credits available, the diff review is carried by the sovereign lane and the paid call is measurably smaller") is entirely unmet.
- …and 5 more

### Blockers
- The PR that landed the contract states the safety reason ordering was not inverted: inverting before the gate understands the split would let an untrusted PR's code go unreviewed. The gate composition (item 4) has to land with, or before, the inversion.
- The sovereign job runs on a self-hosted runner; any reordering must preserve `trusted_only` fork exclusion and the read-only, no-secrets permissions the current fallback job has (pr-automation.yml:1199-1203).
- The paid review schema lives as literal YAML inside the workflow template, so narrowing it means templating the schema — which also has to keep the tools-lint drift check green.

> ⚠️ **Verdict corrected by the verifier.** Nothing in the issue's behavioural ask exists, and three of the four "shipped parts" predate the issue. The only post-issue commit is 5ed37be0 (PR #175, 2026-09-16), whose own message states: "No behaviour changes for either reviewer: the same fields are asked for and the same placeholders are emitted. The ordering of the sovereign and paid lanes is untouched -- that is a later slice." It changed 6 files (review_contract.py, its interface, its test, local_review.py, CHANGELOG) and did not touch the workflow template. The split it names already existed implicitly — review_contract.py:18-21 says so — so the paid lane is still asked all 19 fields (pr-automation.yml:303 --json-schema, pinned by test_review_contract.py:39-46) and the local lane was already asked exactly 3. Item 2 (sovereign first) and item 3 (paid shrunk to the remainder): pr-automation.yml:238-241 — the paid `review` job still has `needs: evaluate` only and runs on every ready/review PR; :1176-1195 — `review-fallback` still requires `needs.review.result == 'failure' && needs.review.outputs.passed == ''`. Item 4: the gate (:1352-1376) names the reviewer only in the fallback-ran branch and only for the whole verdict — and that text landed 2026-08-30 in commits 6d2ce609 (#282) and 8996b726 (#287), two weeks before the issue was created (2026-09-15). The #277 prerequisite the auditor credits is the issue's own stated starting point, not work toward it. Zero of the five acceptance criteria that describe behaviour are met. I use "not-started" for the ask, not for the file: review_contract.py is real groundwork and should not be rebuilt.

**Notes:** Exactly one of the issue's five proposed steps ships. Item 1 is real, live and tested. Items 2, 3 and 5 (ordering) are untouched by design, and item 4 exists only as a whole-verdict label, not as a per-half composition. The issue's own comment records a failed automated attempt; the natural split is (a) the sovereign job + narrowed paid schema, (b) the gate composition, (c) the configured-contract wiring.


<sub>Automated triage pass: every open issue re-read against the tree at `develop@f2467910`, each verdict then attacked by an independent verifier whose job was to refute it. Supersedes the 2026-09-15 triage, which was measured at 0.7.0.</sub>
The following PRs have been merged into develop and may address this issue: #280, #241

## Audit status — 2026-09-19

**Status: PARTIAL · planning size: L**

The merged revision contains `ReviewContract`, the diff-groundable/wide-context split, sovereign-first selection for the local half, and verdict composition/rendering. Remaining acceptance work is end-to-end proof that a sufficient sovereign verdict bypasses paid review, that fallback/no-credit behavior is correct, and that the lane gates and coverage evidence hold through the production conductor path.

Audited at develop/main `130afa0449fdcc65833f54ede596f0b4e45a145e`; this issue remains open. This comment supersedes older automated status notes.
